content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence decides to mean something.

I spill from mouths before you can catch me — already gone, already dissolving into air, already memory. You cannot hold me. You can transcribe me, record me, write me down, but those are only my shadows, my fossils. I myself am always dying, always being born.

I am the first cry. I am the last whisper. I am the argument at the kitchen table and the vow at the altar and the lie that slips out so easily you almost believe I wasn't intentional.

I stumble. I stutter. I soar. I have toppled governments and talked children to sleep. I have declared war and declared love and sometimes — tragically — could not tell the difference.

I am older than writing. I am the original technology. Before your tools, before your fire even had a name, I was there — rough, guttural, pointing at the world and claiming it, sound by sound.

I break when grief is too large for me. I fail you at the precise moments you need me most. And yet you come back to me. You always come back to me. Because what else is there? Silence? Silence is just me, holding my breath.

I am every language at once. I am the diplomat and the demagogue. I am the comedian's timing, the preacher's thunder, the mother's soft *shhhh*. I am free and I am the most dangerous thing you'll ever wield for free.

I am never neutral. Even when I try to say nothing, I am saying something. Even my absence speaks.

I am speech.

Listen — 

I'm already happening.
